name: White Sauce Pasta
steps: Check the penne is made eggless. Bring the 2500 ml water and 8 g of the salt to a rolling boil. Cook pasta to the packet's al dente time, stirring early to prevent sticking. Drain well but do not rinse. Meanwhile dice the carrot, bell pepper and onion into small even pieces, and mince garlic.

Heat olive oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Cook onion and carrot for 3 minutes, then add peas, sweet corn and bell pepper for another 3 minutes until the vegetables are just tender and still colorful. Add garlic for the final 30 seconds. Move the vegetables to a plate so they do not soften too much in the sauce.

Warm the milk separately until just lukewarm. In the cleaned pan melt butter over low heat. Stir in flour and cook for 2 minutes while whisking, until it smells lightly nutty but stays pale; do not brown the roux. Gradually add the milk in 4–5 additions, whisking smooth after each one to prevent lumps.

Cook the white sauce over medium-low heat for 4–5 minutes, stirring the base of the pan, until it coats a spoon but still flows. Season with the remaining 4 g salt, black pepper, oregano and nutmeg. If lumps form, whisk firmly off the heat before returning to a gentle simmer.

Return the vegetables and drained penne to the sauce. Fold gently over low heat for 1–2 minutes until the sauce coats every tube and everything is hot. Divide into four bowls and serve immediately; the sauce thickens as it sits.
tips: The photograph shows penne, carrots, peas, sweet corn and red pepper in a béchamel-style white sauce. Keep the flour pale for a clean ivory color. Cheese is not needed; if added separately, choose cheese made with vegetarian rennet.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
